subject: Tenant tether + egress fallback design review
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sara White <sara.white@finexa.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant tether + egress fallback design review

Hi Sara / Finexa networking team,

Thanks again for the session this morning. Per our notes I'm sending the current diagrams and a short readout for the control-plane/data-plane separation and the proposed egress failover behavior for your on-prem VPC clusters. Attachments: vpc_tether_diagram_v3.png (logical topology) and egress_playbook_draft.pdf (failover decision tree + NAT/proxy behavior).

High-level decisions we want to validate with you before we lock the runbook:
- Control plane (RPCs, provisioning, health checks) will run over the private control channel (mTLS) terminated at Redwood's control endpoints in your VPC; those endpoints will only accept connections from the tenant management subnet.
- Data plane inference traffic originates from tenant worker pods and will egress through your tenant NAT. If local NAT capacity or upstream peering fails, traffic will fail over to a regional egress proxy cluster (regional fabric) via preconfigured BGP-over-IPsec path.
- KMS: You retain key ownership for inference-data-at-rest keys (customer-managed CMKs). Redwood will hold an encrypted key blob for session metadata; audit logs for all DEK operations are pushed to your S3-compatible audit bucket.

Open questions we flagged during the call (please confirm):
1) Acceptable RTO/RPO for control-plane connectivity loss. Our fallback will keep control-plane traffic queued for 60s before rejecting requests — fine?
2) Whether Finexa requires a documented chain-of-custody report for key access; if so we will include the KMS choreography artifact (kms_key_ownership_table.csv) in the compliance bundle.
3) MTU constraints on your edge fabric: we propose 1460 for all encapsulated paths to avoid PMTU issues.

Ask: can you review the two attachments and reply with redlines by EOD Thursday? If useful, propose a 30-minute follow-up to finalize decisions.

Thanks,
Sean

On 2026-05-19 09:15, Sean Gallagher wrote:
> High-level decisions we want to validate with you before we lock the runbook:
> - Control plane ...
> - Data plane inference traffic ...

Quick technical notes and risks from infra:
- BGP failover: we need explicit AS-path preferences and an iBGP overlay between your edge routers and the regional egress cluster. If Finexa cannot accept third-party ASN peering, we will present an alternative using an IPsec tunnel with static routes.
- KV cache warming: when tethered nodes fail over to regional egress, KV cache miss patterns spike. Recommend a short-lived KV pre-warm (per-tenant warm-window) triggered by stateful probe during handoff. I've marked this on vpc_tether_diagram_v3.png (layer: cache-warm suggestion).
- MTU: +1 on Sean's proposal. Also confirm whether any on-prem middleboxes reframe TCP MSS (some enterprise firewalls do).
- Observability: we should push a packet-level flow log for 72 hours post-failover to Finexa's audit bucket for forensic tracing. This should be a required acceptance item for QA.

I'll add two small annotations to the diagram and push a lightweight runbook excerpt (runbook_canary.txt) into Confluence for your review.

-- Jonas
Jonas Weber
Staff Network Architect, Redwood Inacks (infra team)

Subject: Re: Tenant tether + egress fallback design review

Thanks Sean and team — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS: Finexa requires a chain-of-custody statement for any customer-managed keys referenced by 3rd parties. The kms_key_ownership_table.csv will be useful; we also need a sample audit record showing the DEK unwrap flow (timestamp, principal, operation). Can Redwood provide a sanitized example?
- Failover observability: we agree to 72-hour packet flow logs for the initial canary. Please confirm retention windows and S3 object prefixes.
- SLA/Reject behavior: Our security team dislikes silent queuing for control plane > 30s. Can Redwood split the difference to 30s queue + explicit retry semantics documented in the playbook?

We can do a 30-minute follow-up Thursday at 10am PT to iterate on the KMS evidence and the playbook thresholds.

Sara White
Head of Platform Engineering, Finexa Health

Subject: Re: Tenant tether + egress fallback design review

Hi all — adding the proposed canary runbook excerpt inline and attaching a text copy (runbook_canary.txt). Key points: 

- Canary window: deploy to 2 nodes in staging -> monitor for 15 minutes for packet loss, 5xx rate, and KV miss spike.
- Failover criteria: if packet loss > 0.5% OR 5xx rate > 0.3% OR KV miss spike > 250% in window, cut traffic to regional egress; keep a copy of flows in the audit bucket.
- Rollback: automatic rollback to local NAT if RTT to regional egress > 200ms or if regional Jitter exceeds baseline by +40%.

I'll update the playbook with the 30s control-plane queue suggestion from Finexa and add a short snippet showing sanitized KMS audit record format — will provide a sample by Thursday morning. Confluence page is updated (link included above).

Tessa Morgan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — quick consolidation and next steps: 

Decisions agreed:
- Control-plane queue window set to 30s (Tessa to update playbook).
- KV pre-warm will be included as an optional canary step; Jonas to add config flags and annotate diagram.
- BGP preference: Finexa will confirm whether 3rd-party ASN peering is allowed; fallback plan = IPsec + static routes if not.
- KMS: Tessa to provide a sanitized DEK unwrap audit sample by Thursday; we will include kms_key_ownership_table.csv in the compliance bundle.

Action owners and timeline:
- Tessa: update egress_playbook_draft.pdf with 30s queue and add sanitized audit example (due 2026-05-21 10:00 PT).
- Jonas: push annotated vpc_tether_diagram_v3.png (cache-warm + BGP notes) and a short MTU note (due 2026-05-21 17:00 PT).
- Finexa (Sara): confirm acceptable 30-minute follow-up slot (we suggested Thu 10am PT) and whether Finexa network will accept ASN peering or prefers IPsec fallback (reply by EOD 2026-05-20).

If we get sign-off on the above, we will lock the canary and run the 48–72 hour observability window next week. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Sean
